questions.question: In the SI units of the Breguet equations, what are the units of the thrust specific fuel consumption ct of a jet and of the power specific fuel consumption c of a propeller engine?
options: ct in 1/s and c in 1/m
both ct and c in 1/s
ct in 1/m and c in 1/s
ct in kg/(N·s) and c in kg/(W·s)
questions.explanation: Both count the weight of fuel burned. Per newton of thrust per second, N/(N·s) = 1/s; per watt of shaft power per second, N/(W·s) = N/(N·m) = 1/m. Treating them as one unit, swapping them, or keeping a mass flow without multiplying by g all give wrong answers.

questions.question: The jet range equation of this page is derived for steady level flight at constant lift coefficient. What else is held constant?
options: The altitude and the thrust specific fuel consumption
The true airspeed and the thrust of the engines
The throttle setting and the true airspeed
The aircraft mass and the altitude
questions.explanation: The derivation holds the altitude (so the density) and c<sub>t</sub> constant, with C<sub>L</sub>. The speed and the thrust then fall as the mass falls, so the pilot throttles back. Holding the speed constant is the form of page 1.6, which needs the aircraft to climb slowly. The mass cannot be constant: it falls as fuel burns.

questions.question: A jet has ct = 2.0 × 10−4 per second and (L/D)max = 16. It starts at 20,000 kg and ends at 16,000 kg. What is its maximum endurance?
questions.explanation: E = (1/c<sub>t</sub>)(L/D)<sub>max</sub> ln(m<sub>1</sub>/m<sub>2</sub>) = (1/2.0 × 10<sup>−4</sup>) × 16 × ln(1.25) = 80,000 × 0.22314 = 17,851 s = 4.96 h. 9.92 h carries the factor 2 of the range equation; 2.15 h uses the base-10 logarithm; 5.56 h uses 0.25 in place of ln(1.25).

questions.question: A jet has the drag polar CD = 0.016 + 0.060 CL2. At what lift coefficient does it get its maximum range?
questions.explanation: Jet range peaks at the largest C<sub>L</sub><sup>1/2</sup>/C<sub>D</sub>, where C<sub>L</sub> = √(C<sub>D,0</sub>/(3K)) = √(0.016/0.180) = √0.0889 = 0.298. 0.516 is √(C<sub>D,0</sub>/K), the best endurance of a jet; 0.894 is √(3C<sub>D,0</sub>/K), the best endurance of a propeller aircraft; 0.0889 forgets the square root.

questions.section: Jets and propeller aircraft side by side
questions.question: Jet range grows as the density falls. Why can a jet not keep its best-range condition all the way up to its absolute ceiling?
options: Full thrust there only equals the minimum thrust, below the best-range thrust
The best-range lift coefficient there is larger than the maximum lift coefficient
Above the tropopause the jet range equation makes range fall with altitude
The thrust specific fuel consumption becomes zero at the absolute ceiling
questions.explanation: At best range the jet needs 4mg√(KC<sub>D,0</sub>/3), which is 1.155 times the minimum thrust 2mg√(KC<sub>D,0</sub>). At the ceiling full thrust only matches the minimum, so the throttle setting for best range passes 1 lower down. The best-range C<sub>L</sub> is the smallest of the three optima, not a large one; range keeps growing as 1/√ρ in the equation; and c<sub>t</sub> is taken constant.

questions.question: A propeller aircraft has η = 0.85, c = 7.5 × 10−7 per meter and (L/D)max = 14, and its mass ratio is m1/m2 = 1.15. What is its maximum range?
options: 963 km
questions.explanation: R = (η/c)(L/D)<sub>max</sub> ln(m<sub>1</sub>/m<sub>2</sub>) = (0.85/7.5 × 10<sup>−7</sup>) × 14 × ln(1.15) = 1,133,333 × 14 × 0.13976 = 2,218 km. 2,380 km uses 0.15 in place of ln(1.15); 2,609 km leaves out η; 963 km uses the base-10 logarithm.

questions.question: A propeller aircraft must stay in the air as long as possible on a fixed load of fuel. How should it fly?
options: At minimum power required, at low altitude
At minimum thrust required, at high altitude
At maximum C<sub>L</sub><sup>1/2</sup>/C<sub>D</sub>, at high altitude
At minimum power required, as high as it can
questions.explanation: A propeller engine burns fuel in proportion to power, so the minimum power required gives the least fuel per second. The endurance equation carries √ρ, and the minimum power required grows with altitude, so low is best. Minimum thrust gives the best propeller range; maximum C<sub>L</sub><sup>1/2</sup>/C<sub>D</sub> gives the best jet range.

questions.section: Jets and propeller aircraft side by side
questions.question: For an aircraft with a parabolic drag polar, which order of best speeds runs from slowest to fastest?
options: Propeller endurance; propeller range and jet endurance; jet range
Jet endurance; propeller endurance; propeller range; jet range
Propeller endurance; jet range; propeller range and jet endurance
Propeller range; propeller endurance; jet endurance; jet range
questions.explanation: Divided by the minimum-thrust speed, the best speeds are 0.760 for propeller endurance (minimum power), 1 for propeller range and jet endurance together (minimum thrust), and 1.316 for jet range. Each step is a factor of 3<sup>1/4</sup>.
